analysis.title: Tech Valuation Risk & UST Refunding / German Retail Sales / US-Canada Deal / ECB's Kazimir
key_insights: Tech is the central equity risk this week after last week's 3.5% fall in tech stocks and a 4.5% decline in hyperscalers. The concern is whether roughly $10 trn of investment through 2032 can generate adequate returns.
US midterms matter for tech. The Texas governor race is worth watching because how much to restrict data centres is one of its main issues.

Wednesday's US quarterly refunding is expected to keep the $125 bn package ($58 bn 3y, $42 bn 10y, $25 bn 30y) for November-January. Guidance on future auction sizes is likely to matter more than the headline sizes.

A benign refunding outcome would signal smaller longer-dated auctions from May 2027 and possibly dropping 20y issuance. A more aggressive alternative discussed in the market would scrap the 20y and cut 30y issuance, replaced by bills, with potentially substantial curve implications.

Central bank calendar: RBA expected to hike 25bp to 4.85% Tuesday. BoE expected to hike 25bp to 4.0% Thursday. Norges Bank expected to hold at 4.5% Thursday. Riksbank expected to hike 25bp to 2%. No SNB action expected, with Swiss CPI expected at 1.2% y/y versus 1.0%.
Friday US payrolls consensus is 65,000 jobs and 4.2% unemployment, with 4.1% possible on rounding. UBS Economics estimates payrolls +65K, private +70K and unemployment 4.14%.

Germany's September retail sales fell 2.0% m/m versus a consensus rise of 0.4%, and fell 2.3% y/y versus an estimate of -0.2%. The Bundesbank flagged that Q3 GDP likely stagnated, and October inflation eased to 2.8% y/y versus a 3.0% estimate.
Trump said a US-Canada trade deal is 'very close' after talks with Carney, a shift from August when negotiations collapsed.
ECB's Kazimir said markets may be underestimating the work needed to bring inflation under control. UBS notes the market already prices 2-plus further hikes, so the remark is exceptionally hawkish.

Brent fell 2.8% to about $110/bbl and WTI fell 3.3% to $100.67/bbl on Iran diplomacy hopes. Nearly 1 billion barrels have drained from global inventories since Hormuz shipping was disrupted, and diesel inventories in some markets are at 35-year seasonal lows.
OPEC+ kept December production targets unchanged. Its Nov. 29 meeting will address 2027 quotas.
Trump said he would become 'Mr. Veto' if Democrats win Congress. Decision Desk HQ forecasts give Democrats an 83% chance of winning the House and 63% of taking the Senate.
The US is promoting a resumption of Russian gas sales to Europe via Ukraine through a US intermediary (WSJ), facing European opposition.
China October official manufacturing PMI fell to 49.3 from 50.1 (49.9 expected) and non-manufacturing fell to 49.7 from 50.2 (50 expected). The RatingDog manufacturing PMI was 52 versus 52.1 prior.

UBS Economics expects the BoE to hike 25bp to 4%, with a hawkish surprise being an 8-1 vote versus 7-2. It expects the Riksbank to hike to 2% and Brazil to cut to 13.5%, though a pause is a risk. Banxico is a close call. UBS rates strategy is received 1y1y Mexico rates.

UBS US Economics expects ISM manufacturing at 54.0 in October versus 54.5 in September, ISM services down 0.4 points to 54.5, and construction spending up 0.2% in September. Nonfarm productivity is estimated up 1.7% over the year through Q3.
A Democratic sweep could produce modest flattening in rates, but markets are increasingly priced for it. A Republican sweep is the more consequential tail risk for long-end yields.
UBS's LLM-based central bank sentiment tracker shows Warsh's October press conference was his most hawkish since taking office, led by growth. Lagarde was less hawkish than in September.

November has averaged a 1.9% S&P 500 gain since 1950, with only one negative November in the past decade. The S&P was higher six months after every midterm since 1950. Low net and multi-year-high gross exposure create short-squeeze risk and scope for a year-end chase.
The SPX one-day implied move for Wednesday fell to 70bp from 90bp. Nov. 6 SPX ATM volatility is near 12, so downside protection is relatively cheap.

Risk Control funds are estimated to sell $75-100 bn on Monday, possibly triggering remaining NQ1 CTA sell triggers. Further Tuesday selling is likely only if SPX falls more than 2%. After that the systematic selling should fade, setting up a sharp recovery.

No hyperscaler posted a positive return after earnings, and Oracle's 10% mid-week rally was erased by Friday. Expect a Monday retest of Friday's lows. Without long-only sponsorship, sustained upside is hard to see. Hyperscalers remain the higher-quality AI asset on a relative basis.
Copper is holding near record highs while the UBS AI power basket and copper equities (COPX) are down around 30%. UBS's Daniel Major attributes this to physical tightness rather than AI narratives.
Rates trading: the oil-rates correlation has broken down and European country spreads are the focus. UBS holds short 5y ASW versus the wings, with scope to buy the belly of the ASW curve.
Rates trading: Germany's 5y is favoured as French budget risk persists. Markets need to price a December ECB hike.
Rates trading: AUD 1s3s flattening can continue, and macro and systematic accounts are receiving curves, including 2s10s, 3s10s and 5s10s.
Gold broke below its uptrend line and through 3940 and 3900, finding support near 3870. A move back above 4000 is needed to ease downward pressure. Next supports are 3605 and 3500.

Euro Stoxx is up 20bp. NDX futures are up 80bp. UBS equity sales positioning shows Financials (up 17%) and Energy (up 17%) as dominant positive tilts, with Consumer Discretionary (down 27%) the biggest underweight.
Kioxia fell just under 16%, and moves of 10% or more have become more common in the past week. China equities rose on reports the regulator met banks and brokers about supporting capital markets.

geopolitical: Iranian and Qatari officials held three consecutive days of talks aimed at ending the conflict with the US and Israel, and Trump told Netanyahu he prefers diplomacy.
Expectations for another round of US-Israeli military action remain heightened.
Hormuz shipping disruption has drained nearly 1 billion barrels from global oil inventories, per ADNOC CEO Al Jaber.
Trump and Carney signalled a US-Canada trade deal is very close, after talks collapsed in August.
The US is promoting Russian gas transit to Europe via Ukraine through a US intermediary, facing European resistance and the EU phaseout plans.
US midterms on Nov. 3 will decide control of Congress, and Trump said he would veto legislation if Democrats win.
French budget talks remain a risk for French government bonds.
OPEC+ meets Nov. 29 on 2027 production quotas.
